items.name: refute
items.description: 🔭 Find signals. 💥 Try to kill them. ✨ Keep what survives. Open-source framework to refute scientific claims, from new exoplanet candidates 🪐 to published papers 📄, with pre-registration 🔒 and blind tests 🙈. AI agents 🤖 and volunteer computing 🌍 on the roadmap.

items.name: exoplanet-classification-ml
items.description: Exploring machine learning methods to classify NASA Kepler exoplanet candidates.

items.name: Stellaris
items.description: ML pipeline applying CNN and gradient-boosted models to NASA Kepler/TESS photometry for exoplanet candidate identification and cross-mission generalisation.

items.name: mcp-exoplanet-archive
items.description: NASA Exoplanet Archive — ~5600 confirmed exoplanets + candidates

items.name: exoplanet_detector_nasa_data
items.description: Exoplanet Detector using NASA Telescope Data: A telescope-agnostic ML system that classifies exoplanet candidates from Kepler & TESS data into Confirmed, Candidate, or False Positive. Includes habitability scoring and a web app for real-time predictions.

items.name: duo-transits
items.description: Recovering orbital periods of TESS duotransit exoplanet candidates (Hawthorn et al. 2024) using newer TESS sectors, aiming for a Research Note of the AAS.

items.name: exosearch-ai
items.description: Machine learning for exoplanet candidate classification and ranking using NASA TESS data

items.name: startrace-ai
items.description: STARTRACE AI is an interactive exoplanet detection dashboard that visualizes stellar light curves to identify potential planetary transits. It supports CSV uploads, interactive graphs, sample data, and downloadable results, with planned integration of automated candidate detection.

items.name: Quantum-Computing-for-Exoplanet-Exploration
items.description: An exploratory project combining quantum computing and space science to investigate potential exoplanet signals using NASA TESS stellar brightness data. Uses Python, Lightkurve, and Qiskit to analyze light curves, identify candidate dimming events, and demonstrate a Grover-style quantum search simulation.

items.name: exoplanet-transit-classifier
items.description: Exoplanet candidate vetting on real Kepler light curves: phase-folds each KOI with its catalog ephemeris, extracts transit-shape features (U vs V, symmetry, odd-even, secondary eclipse) and classifies confirmed planets vs false positives with a Random Forest.

items.name: open-exoplanet-discovery-lab
items.description: Open exoplanet-discovery laboratory for transit and radial-velocity signals, candidate testing, public data and reproducible detection workflows. Uses reproducible numerical experiments, parameter exploration and quantitative scientific visualization.

items.name: hwo-target-evidence-atlas
items.description: Source-linked Habitable Worlds Observatory target-evidence atlas for organizing candidate-star and exoplanet context, mission-relevant evidence, provenance, diagnostics and explicit measurement limits for future direct-imaging studies.

items.name: finding-earth-2
items.description: Archive-driven, reproducible search for Earth-like exoplanets using public catalogues, habitable-zone filters, planetary parameters, Bayesian reasoning, provenance checks and interactive visual analysis to narrow thousands of records into high-interest candidates.

items.name: Hybrasil
items.description: Hybrasil is a map of every known Exoplanet and Star System with a planet or planet candidate out to 100 ly.

items.name: Using-ML-for-Rapid-Validation-of-Exoplanet-Candidates
items.description: Input_data, processing code and output files

items.name: ExoHunt
items.description: An open-source project for exoplanet data analysis and candidate discovery

items.name: Exoplanets
items.description: My TESS exoplanet work, including candidate searches, transit analysis, false-positive checks, and follow-up.

items.name: exoplanet-detection-hybrid-ensemble-
items.description: Classifying Kepler exoplanet candidates vs. false positives with Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost and a soft-voting hybrid ensemble (NASA Exoplanet Archive KOI data).

items.name: kepler-exoplanet-analysis
items.description: Statistical and multivariate analysis of NASA Kepler exoplanet candidates: hypothesis tests, PCA, correspondence and canonical correlation analysis, clustering

items.name: Exoplanet-Transit-Classifier
items.description: End-to-end machine learning pipeline for detecting exoplanet transit candidates in NASA TESS light curves.

items.name: stellarchart
items.description: Stellarchart — Identify potential exoplanet candidates from raw light curve data through natural language interaction.. Independent MVP inspired by I Think I Found A Planet.

items.name: exoplanet-classification
items.description: #1 Kaggle Exoplanet Classification solution | End-to-end machine learning pipeline for identifying exoplanet candidates from astronomical data.

items.name: exoplanet-transit-classifier
items.description: Deep Learning pipeline for Exoplanet Transit Classification using NASA Kepler light curves, PyTorch, dual-view CNNs, Candidate Ranking, Scientific Scoring, Explainable AI, and an Interactive Dash Dashboard.

items.name: exoplanet
items.description: A student-friendly, production-ready demo that predicts whether a Kepler signal is an exoplanet CANDIDATE or a FALSE POSITIVE.

items.name: TESS-Exoplanet-Finder
items.description: Independent pipeline for finding and vetting exoplanet candidates in NASA TESS light-curve data — automated BLS/TLS period search, multi-sector detrending, and transit vetting against false positives (stellar variability, flares, eclipsing binaries).

items.name: EXONOVA
items.description: EXONOVA — An AI-powered exoplanet detection and visualization platform built with React, TypeScript, Three.js, Flask, and Machine Learning. Explore planetary systems through interactive 3D visualizations and analyze exoplanet candidates using ML.

items.name: bayesianexoplanets.github.io
items.description: Repository of independently verified exoplanets from the TESS and Kepler mission. In addition to fitted planetary properties, we also provide the p-value of every candidate based on the Null Signal Template developed in [Robnik et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.17565).

items.name: kepler-exoplanet-classifier
items.description: Decision Tree Classifier for Kepler exoplanet candidates. Predicts confirmed/candidates/false-positive status from the NASA Kepler cumulative dataset, with accuracy evaluation and a confusion matrix heatmap.

items.name: EXOKAN
items.description: Interpretable exoplanet candidate classification using KAN on NASA Kepler data with Random Forest & XGBoost baselines, feature explanations, and a Streamlit web app.

items.name: exotriage_project
items.description: AI classifier that triages NASA Kepler/TESS exoplanet candidates as confirmed, candidate, or false positive, with an explanation for every call. Trained on physical transit parameters only — not the pipeline's own vetting flags — for a more honest result.
